records.summary: 2183 Mission St sits in the Mission Street NCT zoning district and inside the Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District. The pathway analysis shows that a Restaurant here is a conditional use, and this is a change of use since the site history shows the space was most recently operated as a fast-food restaurant (legal nonconforming use, last approved 2010). The block is extremely dense: 26 food & drink businesses within 500 ft, 5 active ABC on-sale licenses within 500 ft, and 48 ABC licenses within 1,000 ft. Planning records show only 6 dated use decisions in the NCT-MISSION district within 1,000 ft over the last 5 years (1 approved, 3 approved with conditions, 2 withdrawn), far too few to calculate an approval rate, but all four approvals involved restaurants or eating places.

flags.flag: Inside the Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District; restaurants serving alcohol must operate as Bona Fide Eating Places and comply with § 202.2(a) operating conditions
NCT-MISSION caps total eating & drinking uses (Restaurants, Limited Restaurants, Bars) at 167 district-wide; records do not show current count
A Restaurant on the first story in NCT-MISSION is a conditional use, requiring Planning Commission approval
Site history shows a legal nonconforming fast-food restaurant use last approved in 2010; no active ABC license on file, so current use status is unclear
Extremely high density: 26 registered food & drink businesses within 500 ft, signaling strong undue-concentration concerns for ABC
Five active ABC on-sale licenses (Types 41, 47) within 500 ft and 48 within 1,000 ft
The one comparable Type 41 approval at 2170 Mission (49 m away, 2023) required § 202.2(a) conditions and Bona Fide Eating Place operation
A 2001 CUA at this address approved demolition of a 1-story retail building and construction of a 6-story mixed-use building with ground-floor retail and office above
The 2018 CUA at 3372 19th St (192 m, NCT-MISSION) for a restaurant was approved with conditions limiting hours to 11am–1:45am, Tues–Sun

data_gaps: The current count of eating & drinking uses in NCT-MISSION against the 167 cap is not shown
No extracted hearing conditions or decision text for the 2001 CUA at this address
ABC license conditions for nearby active licenses are not exposed
The records do not confirm what use currently occupies 2183 Mission St (last restaurant approval was 2010)

comparables.why_comparable: Type 41 ABC license referral for a restaurant at 2170 Mission (49 m away, same NCT-MISSION zoning, same block, decided Feb-Mar 2023). This is an agency referral for an existing restaurant adding beer and wine service, not a full conditional use hearing.
comparables.key_takeaway: Planning approved the Type 41 for a restaurant in the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD, explicitly requiring the business to operate as a Bona Fide Eating Place and comply with Planning Code § 202.2(a) conditions. Agency referrals show Planning applies § 202.2(a) to all alcohol-serving restaurants in the SUD, even for continuations.

comparables.why_comparable: Full conditional use authorization to legalize a restaurant (Bissap Baobab) at 3372 19th St (192 m, NCT-MISSION zoning) that filed Sept 2018 and was approved March 2019 with 14 conditions. This is a use-decision hearing, the type 2183 Mission would face.
comparables.key_takeaway: The only recent CUA for a restaurant in NCT-MISSION within 1,000 ft was approved with conditions but took six months from filing to approval. Key conditions included hours limited to Tues–Sun 11 a.m.–1:45 a.m., soundproofing, odor control, sidewalk maintenance within a one-block radius, and a community liaison requirement. Extended late-night hours (until 1:45 a.m.) were permitted.

comparables.why_comparable: CUA to establish a new restaurant in a vacant commercial space at 600 South Van Ness (191 m, UMU zoning, Mission area), filed March 2018, approved Aug 2018 (5.5 months). This represents a change-of-use approval in the Mission neighborhood subject to Mission 2016 Interim Zoning Controls.
comparables.key_takeaway: Change-of-use CUA for a new restaurant in the Mission area was approved without extracted conditions within 5.5 months. UMU zoning treated restaurants more favorably than NCT-MISSION, but the case shows Planning approved new restaurant concepts during the Mission Interim Controls period.

comparables.why_comparable: DPH referral for a continuation restaurant use at 3382 18th St (18 m away, NCT-MISSION zoning, essentially next door), approved Jan 2021 citing Planning Code §§ 754 and 249.60. This is the closest comparable geographically.
comparables.key_takeaway: Planning approved a restaurant continuation at the property immediately adjacent (18 m) under § 754 (NCT-MISSION restaurant rules) and § 249.60 (Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD rules). Agency referrals for continuations are routinely approved; a change of use triggers a conditional use hearing.

comparables.why_comparable: Agency referral approving a Limited Restaurant (Ramenwell) at 3378 18th St (31 m, NCT-MISSION) as an existing permitted use under § 754 and the Mission Alcohol SUD rules (§§ 781.8 and 249.60), approved Aug 2018.
comparables.key_takeaway: Planning approved a limited restaurant very close by (31 m) within the Mission Alcohol SUD, citing both the NCT-MISSION district rules (§ 754) and the Special Use District overlay (§§ 781.8, 249.60). Limited restaurants face fewer hurdles than full restaurants, but the case confirms the dual-layer review within the SUD.

comparables.why_comparable: Type 41 ABC referral at 3378 18th St (31 m, NCT-MISSION) for a continuation of an existing restaurant use, approved April 2018. Same concept (restaurant with beer/wine) at nearly the same location.
comparables.key_takeaway: Planning approved a Type 41 license for a restaurant continuation 31 m away as an agency referral in three weeks. Continuations are fast-tracked; a new restaurant filing as a change of use will face the full conditional use process with a Commission hearing.

comparables.why_comparable: Type 47 (full-liquor) ABC referral for a restaurant at 2293 Mission St (186 m, NCT-MISSION), approved Sept 2020 as a continuation under § 754. Illustrates how alcohol licenses are handled within the district.
comparables.key_takeaway: Planning approved a Type 47 full-bar license for an existing restaurant 186 m away under § 754 as an agency referral. Full-liquor licenses are permitted for restaurants in the Mission Alcohol SUD if the restaurant operates as a Bona Fide Eating Place; the concept's Type 41 is less restrictive.

comparables.why_comparable: Health department referral for a full-service restaurant at 2152 Mission St (63 m, NCT-MISSION), approved Nov 2018 (filed April 2017) as a continuation under §§ 790.92 and 712.42. This referral took 19 months, unusually long for an agency matter.
comparables.key_takeaway: A restaurant continuation 63 m away was approved but took 19 months from filing to approval—an outlier timeline for an agency referral, suggesting administrative delays or incomplete submissions. Highlights the importance of complete plan sets and proactive coordination with all referral departments.

patterns.pattern: All recent restaurant approvals in the Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District—whether agency referrals or conditional use authorizations—require compliance with Planning Code § 202.2(a) conditions and Bona Fide Eating Place operation. No exceptions were granted.

Continuation of an existing restaurant use within NCT-MISSION is approved as an agency referral under § 754, typically within 2–4 weeks. A change of use from a different prior use (e.g., fast food, retail) requires a conditional use authorization heard by the Planning Commission.

Conditional use authorizations for new or legalized restaurants in NCT-MISSION took 5–6 months from filing to approval (2018–2019 cases). Both were approved, one with standard conditions and late-night hours.

Standard conditions for restaurant CUAs include hours limits, soundproofing requirements, odor control, sidewalk and litter maintenance within a one-block radius, garbage/recycling storage, and appointment of a community liaison officer.

Type 41 (beer and wine) ABC referrals for existing restaurants in NCT-MISSION are routinely approved by Planning as agency matters within 2–4 weeks, citing § 754 and the Mission Alcohol SUD. Type 47 (full bar) referrals are also approved for restaurants meeting Bona Fide Eating Place standards.

The Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD overlay (§§ 249.60, 781.8) applies to all alcohol-serving eating and drinking uses on this corridor. Planning explicitly cites both the base NCT-MISSION rules (§ 754) and the SUD provisions in every alcohol-related approval.

No restaurant applications in NCT-MISSION within 1,000 ft were denied over the last five years in the available records. The two withdrawals in the district-wide summary are not represented among these nearby candidates.

approval_signals: Continuation of an existing restaurant use, even after change of ownership or entity
Operating as a Bona Fide Eating Place with food service as the primary use and alcohol incidental to meals
Compliance with Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD § 202.2(a) conditions (no take-out alcohol, table service for alcohol, kitchen open during all alcohol service hours)
Type 41 beer-and-wine license rather than full bar (Type 47/48)
Standard soundproofing, odor control, and sidewalk maintenance commitments in CUA applications
Appointment of a community liaison officer to address neighbor concerns
denial_signals: No denials appear in the nearby record set; withdrawal reasons are not stated in the summary

risk.concept_summary: A full-service restaurant with full kitchen, beer and wine service (ABC Type 41), approximately 50 seats and 5 employees, tenant improvements and exterior signage, at 2183 Mission St in the Mission Street NCT zoning district.

overall.next_step: Obtain written confirmation from SF Planning that the district-wide cap of 167 eating and drinking uses is not exceeded, then file a Conditional Use Authorization application under Planning Code § 303 for the Restaurant use.

approvals.summary: A Restaurant here requires Conditional Use Authorization under the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD (§ 249.60(f)(1)) and NCT-MISSION district rules (§ 754); the district caps total eating and drinking uses at 167, but the records do not show the current count.

findings.text: Planning Code § 249.60(f)(1) requires Conditional Use for any proposed Restaurant in the sub-area of the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD east of the western Mission Street NCT boundary and north of Cesar Chavez; zoning district NCT-MISSION lies inside that sub-area.

NCT-MISSION § 754 Table 754 Note 7 caps eating and drinking uses (Restaurants, Limited Restaurants and Bars) at 167 district-wide; a new one is not permitted if it would exceed the cap, but the records do not show how many currently exist.

Site history shows the address was last approved in 2010 as a legal nonconforming self-service restaurant use, and in 2008 as a large fast-food restaurant; no ABC licence is active at 2183 Mission St as of November 2023.

The nearest comparable CUA for a restaurant in NCT-MISSION (3372 19th St, 192 m away) filed in September 2018 and was approved in March 2019, taking six months, with conditions including hours limited to Tuesday–Sunday 11 a.m.–1:45 a.m., soundproofing, odor control, sidewalk maintenance and a community liaison.

Four of six dated decisions in NCT-MISSION within 1,000 ft over the last five years were approved (N = 6: 1 approved, 3 approved with conditions, 2 withdrawn); the base is too small to calculate an approval rate, but all four approvals involved restaurants or eating places.

approvals.summary: The status of the ABC Type 41 licence is insufficient information because the description does not state whether the licence will be obtained new or transferred, and census tract 208.02 is over-concentrated with 22 active on-sale licences against 10 authorised.

findings.text: Census tract 208.02 has 22 active on-sale retail licences against 10 authorised as of ABC's September 2026 census tract authorisations; the tract is over its authorised number and state law tests new licences and transfers for undue concentration.

The description does not state how the Type 41 licence will be obtained (new application or transfer from another owner or location), so the rules cannot determine which ABC licence requirements apply.

ABC will refer the licence application to SF Planning and the Police Department for review; Planning approved a Type 41 for a restaurant at 2170 Mission St (49 m away) in February–March 2023, requiring Bona Fide Eating Place operation and § 202.2(a) conditions.

Planning Code § 249.60(d) mandates that all liquor establishments in the Mission Alcohol SUD comply with § 202.2 operating conditions, and new or relocated establishments must provide outside lighting, keep window signage to 33% and maintain 50% clear glazing on street-facing facades.

approvals.summary: A health permit to operate is allowed: it is issued after plan check and pre-opening inspection without a discretionary hearing, and DPH will refer the application to Planning for zoning review.

findings.text: Every food or drink business in San Francisco needs a health permit to operate, issued by the Department of Public Health after plan check and a final inspection; it is not a discretionary hearing approval.

DPH plan check for a new restaurant carrying tenant improvements costs $2,207 (8 hours at $276/hour) as of FY 2026–27, and the permit to operate application fee is $470 including the initial inspection; the annual licence fee for restaurants is $0 for 2026–28.

The DPH permit application is referred to Planning for zoning sign-off; nearby restaurant referrals at 3382 18th St (18 m) and 2170 Mission (49 m) were approved within 1–4 weeks as continuations of existing restaurant uses.

approvals.summary: A building permit with change of use requires further review: tenant improvements converting the space to restaurant use need DBI plan approval and conformance with the Planning Code before issuance, and a change of occupancy may be required.

findings.text: The concept describes tenant improvements and the pathway analysis concludes this is a change of use; San Francisco Building Code § 106A.1 requires a building permit for tenant improvements and any change of use or occupancy.

Planning Code § 175 requires that every building permit application be referred to Planning for zoning review, and the permit cannot be issued until Planning confirms the project conforms with the Planning Code.

The Building Code classifies a restaurant or bar as Assembly Group A-2 if the occupant load is 50 or more, or Group B if fewer than 50; the description does not state whether the occupant load is above or below 50, so the proposed occupancy group is not established.

The existing occupancy group of the space is not shown in public records; only an architect's review of plans or an inspection can establish the current occupancy, so whether a change of occupancy is required is not established.

Building permit fees are a percentage of construction valuation; for a restaurant kitchen build-out with hood, finishes and ADA upgrades, expect $800–$15,000 depending on scope, plus separate electrical, plumbing and mechanical permits pulled by licensed subcontractors.

expected_conditions.condition: The restaurant shall operate as a Bona Fide Eating Place with alcohol served only incidental to meals, at tables or sit-down counters by employees, and the kitchen open during all hours alcohol is served.
expected_conditions.basis: Planning Code § 249.60(b)(1)(A) requires Bona Fide Eating Place operation for restaurants serving alcohol in the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD. The nearest Type 41 approval at 2170 Mission St (49 m, 2023) explicitly required Bona Fide Eating Place operation and § 202.2(a) compliance.

expected_conditions.condition: No take-out sales of alcoholic beverages; alcohol may only be consumed on the premises. The restaurant must maintain a dedicated eating area with tables and chairs.
expected_conditions.basis: Planning Code § 202.2(a) conditions apply to all liquor establishments in the Mission Alcohol SUD per § 249.60(d). Every recent agency referral for a Type 41 in the district cites § 202.2(a) compliance as a condition.

expected_conditions.condition: Provide outside lighting at the entrance, keep window signage to 33% of window area, and maintain 50% clear glazing on all street-facing facades.
expected_conditions.basis: Planning Code § 249.60(d) mandates these requirements for all new, relocated or expanded liquor establishments in the Mission Alcohol SUD, in addition to the § 202.2 conditions.

expected_conditions.condition: Hours of operation limited, likely to close by midnight or 1 a.m. on weekdays and possibly 1:45 a.m. on weekends, subject to Planning Commission discretion.
expected_conditions.basis: The 2018 CUA at 3372 19th St (192 m, NCT-MISSION) for a restaurant was conditioned to operate Tuesday–Sunday 11 a.m.–1:45 a.m. Hours are a standard condition in restaurant CUAs; expect Planning to impose limits based on the neighborhood context.

expected_conditions.condition: Soundproofing and noise insulation so that incidental noise is not audible beyond the premises, and fixed-source equipment noise does not exceed SF Noise Ordinance decibel levels.
expected_conditions.basis: Standard condition in the 2018 CUA for a restaurant in NCT-MISSION (3372 19th St); Planning applies this to all eating and drinking uses in mixed-use buildings or near residential uses.

expected_conditions.condition: Odor control equipment installed and maintained to prevent noxious or offensive odors from escaping the premises; compliance with Bay Area Air Quality Management District standards.
expected_conditions.basis: Standard condition in the 2018 NCT-MISSION restaurant CUA. Full cooking (fryers, grills, hood) triggers this requirement in every restaurant approval in San Francisco.

expected_conditions.condition: Maintain the building entrance and all sidewalks abutting the property in clean and sanitary condition, and monitor the sidewalk within a one-block radius daily during business hours to remove litter.
expected_conditions.basis: Standard condition in the 2018 NCT-MISSION restaurant CUA and cited as a § 202.2(a) requirement for eating and drinking uses. Planning applies this to all alcohol-serving establishments.

expected_conditions.condition: Appoint a community liaison officer to address concerns from nearby property owners and occupants; provide written notice of the liaison's name and contact information to Planning and registered neighborhood groups.
expected_conditions.basis: Standard condition in the 2018 NCT-MISSION restaurant CUA. Planning routinely requires a community liaison for new restaurants and bars in the Mission to manage operational issues and neighbor relations.

expected_conditions.condition: Garbage, recycling and compost containers kept within the premises and hidden from public view, placed outside only when serviced; comply with DPW disposal and recycling guidelines.
expected_conditions.basis: Standard condition in the 2018 NCT-MISSION restaurant CUA and a universal requirement for all San Francisco food establishments under DPH and DPW regulations.

expected_conditions.condition: Validity period of three years from CUA approval to obtain a building permit and commence construction or the approved use.
expected_conditions.basis: Standard condition in every San Francisco CUA; Planning Code § 303(c) authorizes the Commission to set time limits, and three years is the default validity term in recent CUA motions.

filing_playbook.action: Confirm with SF Planning in writing that the district-wide cap of 167 eating and drinking uses in NCT-MISSION is not exceeded.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Email or call a Planning Department zoning planner and request written confirmation of the current count of Restaurants, Limited Restaurants and Bars in the NCT-MISSION zoning district against the cap of 167 in Planning Code § 754 Table 754 Note 7. Ask whether a new restaurant at 2183 Mission St would be permitted under the cap. Request a Letter of Determination or email confirmation before filing the CUA application, because the cap is a threshold question that can make the use not permitted.

filing_playbook.action: Form the legal entity with the California Secretary of State and obtain a federal EIN from the IRS.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: File LLC Articles of Organization (LLC-1, $70) or Articles of Incorporation (ARTS-GS, $100) with the California Secretary of State online at bizfile.sos.ca.gov. Within 90 days file the Statement of Information ($20 for LLC, due every 2 years; $25 for corporation, due yearly). Once the entity is registered, apply for a federal Employer Identification Number (EIN) free at irs.gov; it is issued immediately online Monday–Friday. The EIN and entity name are needed for the business registration, bank account, lease and every other permit.

filing_playbook.action: Register the business with the SF Treasurer & Tax Collector and file a Fictitious Business Name statement with the County Clerk.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Register online at sftreasurer.org/business to obtain a Business Account Number (BAN); the fee is tiered by gross receipts (e.g., $55 up to $100k, $625 at $1–1.5M for 2026–27). The BAN is required by every city department. Then file a Fictitious Business Name (DBA) statement with the SF County Clerk in person or by mail ($60–$120), publish it once a week for four weeks in a court-approved newspaper, and file proof of publication within 45 days. Banks and ABC need the filed FBN statement.

filing_playbook.action: Obtain a California Seller's Permit from CDTFA and register as an employer with EDD.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Register for a seller's permit at onlineservices.cdtfa.ca.gov; it is free and often issued the same day. ABC will not issue a liquor licence until the seller's permit exists. Then register as an employer at edd.ca.gov/e-services (free, within 7 days) and set up workers' compensation insurance with a licensed carrier or State Fund before hiring anyone. CDTFA may request a security deposit depending on projected taxable sales.

filing_playbook.action: File a Conditional Use Authorization application with SF Planning for the Restaurant use under Planning Code § 303.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Submit the CUA application through the Planning Department's online portal or in person at 49 South Van Ness. The filing fee is approximately $3,150 (2026–27 CPI-adjusted rate for a no-construction CUA; fees rise with construction cost). Attach a detailed project description stating the square footage, occupant load, hours of operation, menu and food service model (Bona Fide Eating Place with table service), floor plans, a description of soundproofing and odor control measures, and a neighborhood outreach plan. State that the restaurant will comply with § 202.2(a) operating conditions and § 249.60(d) facade and lighting requirements. Planning will schedule a pre-application meeting, route the application to Police and other departments, post a 300-foot mailed notice and schedule a Planning Commission hearing. Budget 5–7 months from filing to hearing.

filing_playbook.action: File DPH plan check for the new restaurant kitchen and finishes while the CUA is pending.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Submit two sets of scaled drawings, interior/exterior photos, a detailed menu and equipment list through the DPH Environmental Health online portal at sfdph.org/dph/EH. The plan check fee is $2,207 (8 hours at $276/hour for a new restaurant, FY 2026–27). DPH reviews the layout, finishes, hand sinks, three-compartment sinks, equipment spacing, ventilation hood and grease interceptor. DPH will refer the application to Planning for zoning sign-off; Planning will hold it until the CUA is approved. Schedule a pre-final inspection at ~80% construction complete and a final inspection at least two weeks in advance, both with your assigned plan reviewer.

filing_playbook.action: File a building permit application with DBI for tenant improvements and change of use, stamped by a licensed architect.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Hire an architect with San Francisco restaurant experience to prepare a full plan set showing the kitchen layout, hood and fire suppression, plumbing, electrical, ADA upgrades, finishes and occupant load calculation. Submit the building permit application online at sf.gov/dbiweb or in person at 49 South Van Ness; DBI will route it to Planning, DPH, Fire, Public Works and other departments. The building permit fee is a percentage of construction valuation ($800–$15,000 depending on scope); electrical, plumbing and mechanical permits are pulled separately by licensed subcontractors. DBI will not issue the permit until Planning confirms the CUA is approved and the project conforms to the Planning Code. File this step in parallel with the CUA and DPH plan check to save time.

filing_playbook.action: Apply for the ABC Type 41 licence after the CUA is approved and the building permit is issued or imminent.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Submit the ABC licence application online at abc.ca.gov or by mail to the San Francisco ABC district office. Attach a copy of the approved CUA, the seller's permit, the lease, the entity documents, a diagram of the premises showing the area where alcohol will be served, and the $1,000–$1,600 application fee. Post the required ABC notice at the premises for 30 days. ABC will refer the application to SF Planning and the Police Department; Planning will confirm that the CUA covers alcohol service and that the restaurant meets Bona Fide Eating Place standards. If the census tract is over-concentrated (it is: 22 active vs. 10 authorised), ABC may require a Public Convenience or Necessity (PCN) finding from Planning or the Board of Supervisors, which can add 1–3 months. Budget 60–120 days if unprotested, longer if a PCN is required or if neighbors protest.

filing_playbook.action: Complete construction, pass all final inspections (DBI, Fire, DPH) and obtain the Health Permit to Operate.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Before opening, schedule and pass the final building inspection, the Fire Department hood and occupancy inspection (if occupant load ≥ 50), the SFPUC FOG grease interceptor inspection, and the DPH pre-opening inspection. DPH issues the Health Permit to Operate ($470 application fee, includes initial inspection; $0 annual licence fee for 2026–28) after confirming the facility matches the approved plans, a certified food safety manager is on staff, and all equipment and finishes are code-compliant. Do not serve food to the public before the permit is issued. Apply for ASCAP and BMI music licences ($300–$2,500 each per year) if playing recorded music or live covers. Set up organics/composting collection with the hauler (SB 1383 compliance).

timeline_cost.notes: The timeline and cost are for the entitlement path approvals when they are granted: Conditional Use Authorization, Health Permit to Operate, and Building Permit with change of use. The 120–300 day range is the time to approval and reflects the CUA as the critical path (5–7 months filing to hearing, typically approved 2–4 weeks after the hearing once the motion is drafted), plus overlapping plan check and building permit review. The building permit is issued after the CUA is approved, and DPH issues the health permit after the final inspection passes. Construction time is not included. The $6,800–$23,000 cost range includes the CUA filing fee (~$3,150), DPH plan check ($2,207), DPH permit to operate ($470), building permit fees ($800–$15,000 depending on construction valuation), Fire place-of-assembly permit if occupant load ≥ 50 ($446–$1,500), and FOG interceptor registration ($0–$500). It does not include construction costs, the ABC Type 41 licence ($1,000–$1,600, state agency, not on the entitlement path because how the licence will be obtained is not known), state and federal registrations ($70–$150 entity formation, $0 EIN and seller's permit), business registration ($55–$700), sign permit ($300–$1,500), music licences (~$600–$5,000/year combined), or professional fees (architect, contractor, expediter). The CUA fee may qualify for a First Year Free waiver if this is a new storefront business in a Priority Equity Geography; confirm eligibility with Planning. ABC review runs in parallel but is not included in the city entitlement path because the alcohol row status is insufficient information.
